messages:
Mia (PM): Heads-up — planning a staggered rollout of API v2 next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Main change is content-negotiation via the `Accept-API-Version` header. Need opinions on org-level pinning and enterprise compatibility.

Sam (Eng): Are we doing header-only routing? Some older SDKs and embedded partners can't set arbitrary headers easily.

Alejandra (Docs): I can draft migration notes and small snippets for curl/JS. Will need the final header examples and any fallback flags.

Alex (Platform): Proposal: gateway-level routing that defaults to v1 for requests without the header. Add an org-pin option so we can keep specific orgs on v1. Start with a 10% global canary for 30m, then ramp.

DevDeployBot: Preflight checks passed. Image: skyline:v2-rc4. Capacity available: 120 GPUs. Healthchecks: OK.

Keegan (Support): We have 3 enterprise customers on locked SDKs (org ids 334, 421, 502). Recommend we pin them to v1 and send comms before any change.

Sam (Eng): FYI v2 changes system-message tokenization slightly — will add temporary compatibility header `X-Allow-V1-Tokenization: true` for fallback if clients need it.

Mia (PM): Decision summary: 1) Gate rollout on header when present, 2) Pin the 3 enterprise orgs to v1, 3) Canary 10% for 30m, restrict to US regions if we see anomalies, 4) Extend change window if we need rollback (target end 03:30 UTC). I'll update release notes.

DevDeployBot: Deploy started. Canary rollout: 10% traffic at 2026-03-24T02:05:00Z.

DevDeployBot: Canary metrics @ +15m: error rate 0.1% (baseline 0.05%), 95th latency +6%. Top traces show spikes in region eu-west-1.

Sam (Eng): Investigating — initial suspicion: KV cache warmup across EU nodes and a cold path in our tokenization layer for some payload shapes.

Alex (Platform): Suggestion: limit the active canary to us-west-2 and us-east-1 while we investigate EU. I'll change the gateway routing accordingly.

DevDeployBot: Adjusting canary: restrict active canary to us-west-2/us-east-1. EU canary instances rolled back to v1. Rebalancing traffic now.

Keegan (Support): Notifying the EU customers that may have seen longer latencies. Holding off on any org-pin changes until stability confirmed.

Sam (Eng): After ~40m, 95th latency back near baseline in the US canary. EU issue looks like cache warmup + a timeout threshold we missed — pushing a small infra tweak to reduce cold-start impact.

Mia (PM): OK to proceed: ramp to 30% over the next hour but keep EU excluded until we validate. Alex, add these rollback criteria to the playbook: auto-roll if error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR 95th latency > +20% for 3m.

Alejandra (Docs): Pushing migration guide + release notes now. Included examples:

curl -H "Accept-API-Version: v2" https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate

// JS SDK example
const res = await fetch('/v2/generate', { headers: { 'Accept-API-Version': 'v2' } });

Also noted fallback header `X-Allow-V1-Tokenization: true` and example gateway pin config.

DevDeployBot: Canary ramp to 30% initiated.

Mia (PM): Follow-ups: create a ticket to audit customer SDKs and owners; set deprecation timeline for v1 at 6 months; Notify account team to prep enterprise comms. Thanks everyone :tada:
